- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is trending up, model often overshoots — cap forecast peak at 1–2% below recent high or align with 10-day moving average.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for such cases.  
- If sentiment shows sharp reversal (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.3 within 3 days), model lags in adjusting — shift forecast 1–3 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.  
- In cases where true price drops sharply after a spike, model often fails to recognize the “mean reversion” — reduce forecast slope after peak by 10–20% for 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3–0.5) and price is flat, model tends to overfit noise — smooth forecast using 5-day moving average or reduce volatility coefficient by 30%.
